description:
## Question

What is the current cost breakdown of a `cachix.yml` run, in numbers? Without a baseline every later decision is guesswork.

Measure, on `x86_64-linux` (a CI-like machine) and locally:
- Wall-clock of `nix eval` over `packages.<system>` — i.e. how expensive is it to merely enumerate/instantiate all 79 packages and their versions? This is the floor cost of any eval-based affected-set mechanism.
- Wall-clock and bytes of the substitution phase on a fully-warm cache (the "we download everything" complaint) — how much of the current run is download vs. build vs. fixed setup (nix-installer, cachix-action)?
- Number of derivations and total closure size for `attrValues packages.<system> ++ attrValues devShells.<system>`.
- How long a single representative package build takes when it is a genuine cache miss.

Record the numbers as a linked asset (markdown under `docs/` or the ticket comment). Later tickets cite them.
title: Baseline: where does CI time actually go today?
